1           The Plaintiffs and Counter-Defendants to the above-entitled action submit this CASE
2    MANAGEMENT STATEMENT & PROPOSED ORDER pursuant to the Standing Order for All
3    Judges of the Northern District of California and Civil Local Rule 16-9.
4    1.     Jurisdiction & Service:

5           Subject Matter Jurisdiction:

6           Plaintiffs contend that this Court has subject matter jurisdiction over Plaintiffs’ claims

7    under 28 U.S.C. §§ 1332, 1367 and 18 U.S.C. §§ 1030, 1836, and 1964(c)-(d).

8           Personal Jurisdiction and Venue:

9           Counter-Defendants Ed Carpenter Racing, LLC (“Carpenter Racing”), Heartland Food

10   Products Group d/b/a TC Heartland, LLC (“Heartland”), and One Motorsports Marketing and

11   Management, LLC (“One Motorsports”) contend that this Court lacks personal jurisdiction over

12   them because none of them are domiciled in the state of California and they have no licenses, real

13   property, bank accounts, corporate records, or places of businesses in California. They also do not

14   direct their activities toward California or purposefully avail themselves of the privilege of

15   conducting activities in California, nor do any of Counterclaimants’ claims arise out of any conduct

16   that occurred in California. Counter-Defendants Carpenter Racing, Heartland, and One

17   Motorsports have filed motions to dismiss on these grounds, among others.

18          Counter-Defendant ARF1 Investment Fund, LLC (“ARF1”) contends that venue is

19   improper because Counterclaimants’ claims against ARF1 arise from an agreement (“ARF1

20   Agreement”) where Counterclaimants and ARF1 agreed that proper venue is in the State of

21   Delaware. Specifically, the ARF1 Agreement states, “[t]his Subscription Agreement will be

22   governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware. The venue for

23   any legal action under this Agreement will be in the proper forum in the State of Delaware.”
     Counter-Defendant ARF1 filed a motion to dismiss on these grounds, among others.
24

            Plaintiffs’ Statement of Facts:
26
            Plaintiffs Team Rossi Motorsports, LLC (“TRM”), Pieter Rossi, and Alexander Rossi,

1    [ECF No. 1]. Pieter Rossi is a principal in TRM and is Alexander Rossi’s father. The Complaint
2    stated causes of action against Defendants Michael Gesser, Alaska Coffee Roasting of Florida,
3    LLC, and Alaska Coffee Roasting, Inc. for breach of contract, intentional interference with
4    prospective economic relations, intentional interference with contractual relations, and

5    defamation per se/libel. [ECF No. 1]. Plaintiffs’ causes of action are restated in the First

6    Amended Complaint for Damages filed January 22, 2025 (“Amended Complaint”). [ECF No.

7    39]. Plaintiffs Amended Complaint more fully sets forth the factual background originally

8    alleged in the Complaint. As demonstrated in the Amended Complaint, Plaintiffs’ causes of

9    action arise principally out of Defendants’ November 29, 2024 letter (“Demand Letter”) sent to

10   ARF1, TRM, Pieter Rossi, and various other third-parties, including Plaintiffs’ partners,

11   investors, and sponsors. The Demand Letter contained and asserted false, defamatory, libelous

12   and disparaging statements related to Plaintiff TRM and, by association, Plaintiffs Pieter Rossi

13   and Alexander Rossi. The false, defamatory and libelous statements contained in the Demand

14   Letter regarding TRM, and by implication and association Pieter Rossi and Alexander Rossi,

15   were communicated to third parties. The Demand Letter also disclosed confidential information

16   of TRM and ARF1 to the third parties.

17          The Demand Letter was sent to the new racing team where Alexander Rossi would be a

18   driver, Carpenter Racing. TRM, Pieter Rossi and Alexander Rossi had established and begun a

19   new business and contractual relationship with Carpenter Racing prior to Carpenter Racing’s

20   receipt of the Demand Letter. Through Carpenter Racing, Alexander Rossi is sponsored by

21   Heartland and its brands Splenda and Java House. The Demand Letter was also sent to

22   Heartland. Warren “Ned” Spieker (“Spieker”) is an independent contractor consultant with TRM

23   and he is a revenue sharing participant in TRM and Class B Member in ARF1. Spieker also
     received the Demand Letter. The Demand Letter was sent to Carpenter Racing, Heartland and
24
     Spieker by Defendants/Counterclaimants to interfere with the prospective economic relations and
25
     contracts that TRM, Pieter Rossi and Alexander Rossi established and maintained with Carpenter
26
     Racing, Heartland and Spieker.

1           The original Counterclaim was filed on January 16, 2025, by Defendants against TRM,
2    Pieter Rossi, Alexander Rossi, One Motorsports, ARF1, Carpenter Racing, Heartland and Spieker.
3    Then, on January 30, 2025, the Counter-Plaintiffs effectively repackaged their Counterclaim and
4    filed their Amended Counterclaim. The same recklessness Defendants exhibited in the November

5    29, 2024 Demand Letter, which precipitated the present controversy, is also displayed in both the

6    Counterclaim and Amended Counterclaim. The Amended Counterclaim is procedurally flawed, is

7    based on inaccurate statements, caused delay, and further harmed Plaintiffs by unnecessarily

8    increasing the cost of litigation. Counter-Plaintiffs have brought the meritless Amended

9    Counterclaim against Carpenter Racing, Heartland and Spieker (collectively the “Third Party

10   Defendants”) for the improper purpose of further intentionally interfering with TRM, Pieter Rossi

11   and Alexander Rossi’s prospective economic relations with the Third Party Defendants, to

12   intentionally interfere with TRM, Pieter Rossi and Alexander Rossi’s contractual relations and to

13   further defame and liable TRM, Pieter Rossi and Alexander Rossi to the Third Party Defendants.

14          Counter-Defendant ARF1’s Statement of Facts:

15          ARF1 is a business investment fund, which was formed in order to fund professional athlete

16   and race car driver, Alexander Rossi, for participation in Formula 1 or another senior level in

17   motorsports. The use of the funds through ARF1 is to provide a portion of the resources necessary

18   to fund Alexander Rossi’s career as a race car driver. ARF1 made an offering for a specified number

19   of Class A and Class B membership units to be purchased by investors. Each potential investor

20   received a private placement memorandum (“PPM” or “ARF1 Agreement”) that described how

21   the funds would be used and how ARF1 would share in all of Alexander Rossi’s earnings during

22   the first ten years that he earns a driver salary, which concludes March 31, 2026. Alexander Rossi’s

23   earnings to be shared with ARF1 include his driver’s salary obtained through driver services
     agreements with race teams, income through merchandise sales and personal endorsements
24
     (personal sponsorships). Investors were cautioned that the purchase of ARF1 membership units
25
     involved “a high degree of risk” and that “only those investors who can bear the loss of their entire
26
     investment should invest in these units,” and that the projections made were forward-looking
27
     statements, not guarantees of an expected return on investment, or any return on investment. The
28

                                                Page 4 of 18
           Case 3:24-cv-09393-WHO             Document 112        Filed 04/22/25      Page 5 of 18




1    investors acknowledged their understanding of the risk of potentially losing their entire investment,
2    that no guarantees were made to them regarding an expected return on their investment and
3    represented that they were suitable investors who could bear such a risk. Investors were
4    additionally informed that the full contents of the PPM were considered confidential information

5    and that by receiving the PPM and signing the subscription agreement contained therein, they

6    acknowledged that the contents of the PPM, including the cost of each unit being offered in the

7    PPM were considered confidential information. The PPM further explained that Alexander Rossi

8    is managed by Team Rossi Motorsports, LLC (“TRM”), and that “TRM is responsible for driver

9    contract negotiations, team selections, race series platform, promotional, and all [public relations]

10   activities.” In its role as manager for Alexander Rossi, TRM engaged in driver services agreements

11   on behalf of Alexander Rossi, with Manor Formula 1 Team (2025) and IndyCar racing teams such

12   as Andretti Autosport (race seasons 2016-2022) and Arrow McLaren (race seasons 2023-2024),

13   and Counter-Defendant Carpenter Racing for the 2025 race season. Lastly, the ARF1 Agreement

14   sets choice of law and venue in the State of Delaware. Defendant Michael Gesser received and

15   signed the PPM and attached it as Exhibit 1 to his Amended Counterclaim.

16          Counter-Defendant Carpenter Racing’s Statement of Facts:

17          Carpenter Racing is in the business of developing, racing, and testing motor vehicles

18   designated for the NTT IndyCar racing series. In September 2024, Heartland Food Products

19   Group, d/b/a TC Heartland, LLC (“Heartland”) and its brands Splenda and Java House joined

20   Carpenter Racing as a sponsor for and of Carpenter Racing and its drivers.

21          Carpenter Racing is one of the eleven full-time teams for IndyCar’s 2025 season. In

22   pursuit of building a winning team, Carpenter Racing entered into a driver services agreement

23   with Team Rossi Motorsports, LLC (“TRM”), Alexander Rossi’s management company (“Driver

24   Agreement”). The Driver Agreement was entered into in September of 2024 and is “[…] to

25   provide the services of Alexander Rossi (‘Driver’), a professional race car driver who has

26   successfully driven race cars of varying types in sanctioned racing series events.”

27          Alexander Rossi then became one of Carpenter Racing’s three drivers for the 2025 IndyCar

28   season. Through this relationship, Carpenter Racing’s partner, Heartland and its prestigious and

20          Counter-Defendant One Motorsports Statement of Facts:

21          One Motorsports is a motorsport management and advisory firm that manages and

22   promotes several talented race car drivers. Pieter Rossi and Alexander Rossi are the principals of

23   One Motorsports and formed the company to help give young, less established race car drivers

24   opportunities to reach the top levels of racing. One Motorsports manages these drivers and

25   provides guidance on long-range career planning, as well as consultation on how to attain the

26   financial backing required to achieve their goals in an otherwise cost-prohibitive sport. One

27   Motorsports also works directly with racing teams and racing series, such as Formula 1, IndyCar

28   and NASCAR, to acquire sponsorships. One Motorsports does not manage the racing career or

4            On or about March 7, 2024, One Motorsports entered into a joint venture agreement (“Joint
